clients.doc: The per-invocation context the shim passes to the handler.

methods.name: log
methods.signature: log(*args: object) -> None
methods.doc: Prints the arguments, separated by spaces, as one line on standard output, which funcd keeps as a log line at level INFO.

methods.name: invoke
methods.signature: invoke(alias: str, payload: Any) -> Any
methods.doc: Calls the function that the link named ``alias`` targets, and returns its result parsed from JSON, or ``None`` when it returns nothing. The target's ``event["data"]`` is ``payload``, except that a dict with a top-level ``"data"`` or ``"specversion"`` key is taken as the whole CloudEvent, so ``event["data"]`` is only its ``"data"`` value: send such a dict inside an envelope, as ``{"specversion": "1.0", "data": payload}``. The link's timeout, 30 seconds by default, bounds the call. Fails with the HTTP status 403 when the function declares no link named ``alias``, 409 when the target serves HTTP, 422 when ``payload`` does not match the target's contract, and the target's status when its handler fails, such as 500.

methods.name: remaining_ms
methods.signature: remaining_ms() -> int | None
methods.doc: The whole milliseconds left before the call's deadline, 0 once it has passed, or ``None`` when the call has none.

clients.name: kv
clients.doc: The key-value tables that the function binds, by alias: read, write and list their keys.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(binding: str, key: str) -> bytes | None
methods.doc: The key's value as bytes, or ``None`` when the key does not exist.

methods.name: get_entry
methods.signature: get_entry(binding: str, key: str) -> KVEntry | None
methods.doc: The key's value with its version, or ``None`` when the key does not exist.

methods.name: get_str
methods.signature: get_str(binding: str, key: str) -> str | None
methods.doc: The key's value decoded as UTF-8 text, or ``None`` when the key does not exist.

methods.name: get_json
methods.signature: get_json(binding: str, key: str) -> object | None
methods.doc: The key's value parsed as JSON, or ``None`` when the key does not exist. Write it with ``put(binding, key, json.dumps(value))``.

methods.name: put
methods.signature: put(binding: str, key: str, value: bytes | str, *, ttl: int | None = None) -> None
methods.doc: Writes the value. ``ttl``, in whole seconds, sets the key's expiry; a put without it leaves the key with none. Only the table's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can write.

methods.name: put_if_absent
methods.signature: put_if_absent(binding: str, key: str, value: bytes | str, *, ttl: int | None = None) -> str | None
methods.doc: Creates the key: its new version, or ``None`` when it exists (an expired key does not).

methods.name: compare_and_set
methods.signature: compare_and_set(binding: str, key: str, value: bytes | str, version: str, *, ttl: int | None = None) -> str | None
methods.doc: Replaces the key while it is at ``version``: its new version, or ``None`` when it is not.

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: delete(binding: str, key: str) -> None
methods.doc: Deletes the key.

methods.name: delete_if
methods.signature: delete_if(binding: str, key: str, version: str) -> bool
methods.doc: Deletes the key while it is at ``version``, as a lease holder releases what it holds: ``True`` when it did.

methods.name: list
methods.signature: list(binding: str, prefix: str = '') -> list[str]
methods.doc: The keys that start with ``prefix``; without a prefix, every key of the table.

clients.name: blob
clients.doc: The Bucket prefixes that the function binds, by alias: read, write, delete and list their objects, whose keys are relative to the binding's prefix.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(binding: str, key: str) -> bytes | None
methods.doc: The object's content as bytes, or ``None`` when the object does not exist.

methods.name: put
methods.signature: put(binding: str, key: str, data: bytes) -> None
methods.doc: Writes the object, replacing any object with that key. ``data`` is at most 64 MiB, and at most the Bucket's ``spec.quota.maxObjectBytes`` when that is set: a larger one fails with the HTTP status 413. Only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can write.

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: delete(binding: str, key: str) -> None
methods.doc: Deletes the object, and fails with the HTTP status 404 when it does not exist. Only the prefix's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can delete.

methods.name: list
methods.signature: list(binding: str, prefix: str = '') -> list[str]
methods.doc: The keys that start with ``prefix``; without a prefix, every key under the binding's prefix.

methods.name: signed_url
methods.signature: signed_url(binding: str, key: str, method: str = 'GET', expiry: str | None = None) -> str
methods.doc: A presigned URL that lets its holder send a ``method`` request for the object until ``expiry`` passes: a duration string such as ``"10m"`` or ``"1h30m"``, in whole seconds from 1s to 168h, or 15 minutes when ``None``. A method other than ``GET``, ``PUT`` or ``DELETE``, or any other expiry, ``""`` included, fails with the HTTP status 400; an ``expiry`` that is not a string raises ``TypeError`` before any request. A ``PUT`` or ``DELETE`` URL needs permission to write the prefix, and a ``PUT`` URL fails with the HTTP status 403 when the Bucket sets ``maxObjectBytes`` or a size quota applies to the Bucket or the prefix, since funcd could not enforce it on the upload. No blob store that funcd opens signs URLs, so a call that passes these checks fails with the HTTP status 503.

clients.name: sql
clients.doc: The SQL databases that the function binds, by alias: ``query`` reads rows, ``query_values`` keeps every column of a join, and ``execute`` writes in one transaction. A call fails with the HTTP status 503 while the database's engine is not Ready, or when a statement runs past funcd's SQL call timeout, 30 seconds by default.

methods.name: query
methods.signature: query(alias: str, sql: str, params: SQLParams | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
methods.doc: Runs one statement that reads, and returns its rows as dicts keyed by column name; with a duplicate column name, the last one wins. ``params`` fill the statement's ``?`` placeholders in order, or its ``:name`` placeholders from one mapping. A statement that writes, or that the database refuses, fails with the HTTP status 400.

methods.name: query_values
methods.signature: query_values(alias: str, sql: str, params: SQLParams | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
methods.doc: Runs one statement that reads, and returns ``{"columns": [...], "values": [[...]]}``: its column names and its rows as lists of values in column order, so every column of a join is kept. ``params`` and failures are as for ``query``.

methods.name: execute
methods.signature: execute(alias: str, sql_or_statements: str | Sequence[SQLStatement], params: SQLParams | None = None) -> Any
methods.doc: Runs one statement, or a list of up to 500 statements, in one transaction that applies all or none of them. Returns the statement's result, or one result for each statement of a list: a dict with ``rowsAffected`` and ``lastInsertId``, and ``columns`` and ``values`` for a RETURNING statement. A statement that the database refuses fails the call with the HTTP status 400. Only the database's owner and the writers that a RolesAssignment names can execute.

clients.name: config
clients.doc: The keys of the ConfigMaps that the function binds, with the values that the worker got when it started. A key that starts with ``FUNCD_`` is left out, since funcd reserves that prefix. A key that a bound Secret also holds is left out too, and ``ctx.secret`` reads the Secret's value. While funcd's S3 gateway runs, a function that binds a Bucket reads the ``AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`` and ``AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`` that funcd issues it, in place of a ConfigMap's.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(key: str) -> str | None
methods.doc: The key's value, or ``None`` when ``list()`` does not include the key.

methods.name: list
methods.signature: list() -> list[str]
methods.doc: The keys of the bound ConfigMaps, sorted, without the keys left out.

clients.name: secret
clients.doc: The keys and values of the Secrets that the function binds, which funcd reads at each ``get`` or ``list``, with no cache, so a changed Secret shows at the next read. A key that starts with ``FUNCD_`` is never read: ``get`` returns ``None`` for it, and ``list`` leaves it out.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(key: str) -> str | None
methods.doc: The key's value, or ``None`` when no bound Secret holds the key, the key starts with ``FUNCD_``, or a bound Secret does not exist. When two Secrets hold the key, the later one in ``spec.bindings.secret`` wins. Fails with the HTTP status 403 when a Policy forbids the function to read a bound Secret.

methods.name: list
methods.signature: list() -> list[str]
methods.doc: The keys that the bound Secrets hold, sorted, except a key that starts with ``FUNCD_``. Fails with the HTTP status 403 when a Policy forbids the function to read a bound Secret, and 404 when a bound Secret does not exist.

methods.name: put
methods.signature: put(binding: str, key: str, value: str) -> None
methods.doc: Writes key in Secret ``binding``, which the function binds and may write: its owner, or a principal a writer role names. Every function that binds it reads the value at its next read.

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: delete(binding: str, key: str) -> None
methods.doc: Removes key from Secret ``binding``, as put may write it; a key the Secret lacks is no error.

clients.name: lake
clients.doc: The Lakes that the function binds, by alias: the address of each Lake's gateway, and the token that the gateway accepts from the function.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(alias: str) -> LakeEndpoint
methods.doc: The gateway of the Lake bound as ``alias``: ``url``, its address as ``host:port``, and ``token``, the token that it accepts from the function. Raises ``KeyError`` naming the alias when the function binds no Lake with that alias.
